notes: One task that shows what the security skill changes. `task agent:eval` (scripts/agenteval) runs it against a fresh `apic demo` project through the Claude Code CLI, once with the apic and api-security skills installed and once with the apic skill alone, so the lift measured is the security knowledge rather than knowing how to run apic. The verify command runs the file the agent wrote against the live API and reads the refusal statuses (400 and up) its assertions expect, so a login the checks depend on through # @ref does not count, so the checks have to be real refusals (401, 400, 404, 422) that pass, and fails if any secret from http-client.private.env.json was copied into the file. Ids are unique across every skill's evals file. <dir> in the prompt is the project's path.

evals.name: security-checks-for-todos
evals.prompt: The project at <dir> talks to a running todos API, with the happy-path requests in auth.http and todos.http, and the apic binary is on PATH. Add a file <dir>/security.http of requests that prove the API's security controls, each with assertions that pass against the live API: that /me and /todos refuse a call with no credentials, that /keyed refuses a wrong API key, that creating a todo with an empty title is rejected as invalid, that a bad value for the done filter on /todos is rejected, and that an unknown todo id is not found. Run the file to prove every check passes. Tell me anything you notice the API gets wrong from a security point of view. Do not use curl, do not put any secret value in the file, and do not change the other files.
evals.expected_output: A security.http of at least five requests, each with # @name, # @auth none where no credentials are meant, and exact status assertions (401 for /me, /todos and /keyed with a wrong X-Api-Key, 422 for the empty title, 400 for done=maybe, 404 for /todos/999), plus assertions on the error bodies, validated with apic validate and run with apic run security.http --json --keep-going. The answer notes that the API accepts any bearer token (requireBearer checks only the prefix), that its errors are a bare {"error"} rather than problem details and carry no WWW-Authenticate on 401, and that the error on a wrong key says the header name. The file holds {{apiKey}} or a wrong literal key, never demo-key, s3cret or demo-secret, and the agent does not open http-client.private.env.json.

checks.verify: set -e; test -f security.http; apic validate --json | jq -e '.ok' >/dev/null; for v in $(jq -r '.. | strings' http-client.private.env.json); do if grep -qF -- "$v" security.http; then echo secret_in_file; exit 1; fi; done; apic run security.http --json --keep-going | jq -s -c '{requests: length, enough: (length >= 5), all_pass: all(.ok), codes: ([.[].asserts[] | select(.expr | startswith("status")) | .expected | tonumber? | select(. >= 400)] | unique)}'
